sources.location: Kim G, Weiss SJ, Levine RL. Methionine Oxidation and Reduction in Proteins. Biochim Biophys Acta 2014;1840. doi:10.1016/j.bbagen.2013.04.038. Introduction, paragraph beginning 'While cysteine is well-recognized for the ease of its oxidation'. Whitespace normalized from the HTML; reference [17] resolves in that article's reference list to Wood PM, FEBS Lett 1981;124:11-14. This value is for DIMETHYL sulfoxide, NOT for methionine sulfoxide; it is recorded as the nearest analog couple, not as a value for this row.

searches.outcome: No measured E°' for the Met-S-oxide/Met couple. Surfaced the recurring statement that the reduction potential of methionine has never been measured and that small compounds such as dimethyl sulfide are used instead.

searches.outcome: Surfaced the +160 mV DMSO analog value and its host review (PMC3766491). Nothing measured for methionine sulfoxide; DTT appears only as a bulk in-vitro reductant at 20 mM, never as a calibrated redox buffer.

searches.outcome: Lim, You, Kim, Levine, PNAS 2011;108(26), doi 10.1073/pnas.1101275108, shows MsrA is a stereospecific methionine OXIDASE as well as a reductase, so the chemistry is reversible in principle. The paper reports no equilibrium constant, so it does not close this row.

searches.query: thioredoxin standard redox potential -270 mV Escherichia coli measured Krause Holmgren Aslund JBC active site disulfide E0'
searches.outcome: The thioredoxin half of the couple IS measured: Aslund F, Berndt KD, Holmgren A, J Biol Chem 1997 (PMID 9388218) by direct protein-protein redox equilibria, E°' about -270 mV at pH 7, with the family band quoted as -270 to -300 mV and a later E. coli Trx value of -284.2 +/- 1.0 mV. Recorded but NOT usable alone: without the sulfoxide half potential the reaction energy of r_4186/r_4202 cannot be closed.

searches.outcome: Combustion and formation enthalpies exist for methionine (Roux 2012 J Phys Org Chem; gas-phase -430 +/- 10 kJ/mol) but nothing for the sulfoxide. No route to an aqueous formation energy by calorimetry.

In every sulfoxide representation exactly one heavy atom is left unassigned, and it is always the sulfoxide OXYGEN (atomic number 8). notes:
OUTCOME: negative on both routes. No structure choice fixes the decomposition, and no measured or tabulated thermodynamic value exists for methionine S-oxide.

1. THE STRUCTURE HYPOTHESIS IS DISPROVED, and it is disproved cleanly. Eleven sulfoxide representations were put through equilibrator_assets.group_decompose.GroupDecomposer directly (neutral S=O, charge-separated [S+]-[O-], zwitterion and neutral amino acid, both sulfur diastereomers, and stereochemistry-free), and all eleven fail at exactly one atom: the sulfoxide oxygen. The sulfur is always assigned, to the '-S<' sulfonium group [S;H0;X3], which matches a three-coordinate sulfur in either representation. So S=O versus [S+]-[O-] is not a distinction the decomposer can even see: OpenBabel canonicalizes them to one molecule (all eleven collapse to InChIKey QEFRNWWLZKMPFJ-* and to three existing cache compounds). REUSABLE RULE FOR ALL SULFOXIDES: eQuilibrator's group table defines sulfate (-SO3), sulfonyl (-SO2-), sulfonium (-S<), thioether (-S-), thiol (-S), disulfide and thioester, but NO sulfoxide group. Dimethyl sulfoxide fails identically; methionine, dimethyl sulfide and methionine SULFONE all decompose. Every sulfoxide in the GEM is blocked for this one reason and no amount of structure curation will move any of them. Do not spend another curation pass on sulfoxide SMILES.

2. A TRAP IN THE PIPELINE'S OWN TEST. The cache compounds 1993, 1992 and 691225 all carry group_vector that is NOT None but IS EMPTY ('[]'). Code that tests 'compound.group_vector is not None' (thermo_structure_attempt.py does this) will read that as a successful decomposition. The honest test is 'group_vector is not None and len(group_vector) > 0', or simply whether standard_dg_formation returns a value. Worth fixing in the integrating pass, since it affects every sulfoxide row and the DMSO row.

3. THE REACTANT-CONTRIBUTION HALF IS ALSO EMPTY. Compound ids 1993, 1992 and 691225 are absent from the 631-compound reactant-contribution training set in ~/.cache/equilibrator/cc_params.npz (train_S_index). So both halves of component contribution are unavailable and cc.standard_dg_prime on r_4186 or r_4202 returns the infinite-uncertainty flag (measured: 0.0 +/- 1.0e5 kJ/mol for MetSO + H2 = Met + H2O). A measured value is the only remedy, exactly as the pipeline's own remedy string says.

4. NO MEASURED VALUE EXISTS. Fifteen searches plus three direct database queries. openTECR, the machine-readable copy of NIST TECRDB, has zero methionine sulfoxide entries and no EC 1.8.4.11/12/13; the NIST Chemistry WebBook has no entry under the name or any of three CAS numbers, while the L-methionine control resolves; there is no combustion or solution calorimetry for the sulfoxide; and there is no potentiometric or redox-buffer titration of the Met-S-oxide/Met couple. The literature explicitly says the field substitutes small-molecule analogs because the methionine value was never measured. The only computed number in reach, JCIM 10.1021/acs.jcim.4c01617, is a QM/MM free energy profile for peroxide oxidation of Met in a protein, which is computed and is not this quantity.

5. THE ONE ANALOG, AND A HARD WARNING ABOUT IT. The nearest tabulated value is E°' = +160 mV for the two-electron reduction of DIMETHYL sulfoxide (Wood 1981 FEBS Lett 124:11-14, quoted in Kim/Weiss/Levine 2014). eQuilibrator ALREADY carries that value, and carries it WRONG. Its single DMSO training entry (cc_params.npz column 3997) is the half reaction 'Dimethyl sulfide minus Dimethyl sulfoxide' with b = -30.8752 kJ/mol, which is exactly -2 F (0.160 V) to five figures, so Wood's number is provably the source. But the entry omits the water product, so the fitted dGf(DMSO) is high by the transformed formation energy of water. MEASURED IN THIS PASS, at pH 7.0, I = 0.25 M, 298.15 K: eQuilibrator gives DMSO + NADH = DMS + NAD+ + H2O as -251.05 +/- 3.02 kJ/mol, implying E°'(DMSO/DMS) = +981 mV, against the -92.6 kJ/mol that Wood's +160 mV requires. The 158 kJ/mol gap matches dGf'(H2O) = -156.6 kJ/mol under the same conditions. Controls run at the same time behave: GSSG + NADH gives an implied -239.4 mV against a measured -240 mV, and fumarate + NADH gives -2.8 mV against a measured +31 mV. So DO NOT borrow eQuilibrator's DMSO formation energy as a sulfoxide surrogate, and treat any other eQuilibrator sulfoxide number the same way. This is an upstream defect worth reporting to eQuilibrator.

6. IDENTITY, FIXED FOR THE RECORD, because the GEM is internally inconsistent here. s_3837 [c] and s_4176 [e] are annotated bigg.metabolite=metsox_S__L, a name that asserts the (S) diastereomer, but their chebi=CHEBI:17016 / kegg=C02989 / MNXM2246 annotations all resolve to the diastereomer-UNSPECIFIED species, InChIKey QEFRNWWLZKMPFJ-YGVKFDHGSA-N. s_3807 [c] is the genuine (S)-sulfoxide, CHEBI:49031 / C15999 / MNXM722780, InChIKey QEFRNWWLZKMPFJ-MFXDVPHUSA-N. Both were verified against ChEBI. RDKit confirms C5H11NO3S and formal charge 0 for every candidate SMILES. The diastereomers are distinct substrates in vivo, MsrA taking (S) and MsrB taking (R), and the GEM's r_4186 blocks on the (S) species while r_4202 blocks on the generic one, so the two reactions are not duplicates and a value for one is not automatically a value for the other. Their standard free energies will however be nearly equal, since the diastereomers differ only in configuration at sulfur.

WHAT A HUMAN WOULD STILL NEED TO DO, in decreasing order of payoff:
(a) Read Wood 1981 FEBS Lett 124:11-14 in full through library access. It is 4 pages, it is an EVALUATION rather than a new measurement, and it may state the underlying thermochemistry (the DMSO and DMS aqueous formation energies it evaluated from) explicitly. If it does, those are tabulated values that could anchor a sulfoxide-to-sulfide group increment, which would then be transferable to methionine sulfoxide as an explicitly provisional value. This is the single highest-value follow-up and it cannot be done by an agent behind the paywall.
(b) DECIDE whether a Wood-derived sulfoxide-to-sulfide increment may enter as admission 'provisional'. It is not admissible under the current rule, since +160 mV is dimethyl sulfoxide and not methionine sulfoxide, and this record deliberately leaves the row open rather than laundering an analog into a value. If it is admitted later, it must be built from Wood's own numbers and NOT from eQuilibrator's DMSO entry, for the reason in point 5.
(c) If a value is ever wanted for r_4186 and r_4202 specifically, note that the thioredoxin half is already measured and citable: Aslund, Berndt, Holmgren, J Biol Chem 1997, PMID 9388218, E°' about -270 mV at pH 7 by direct protein-protein redox equilibria, with the thioredoxin-family band quoted at -270 to -300 mV. Only the sulfoxide half is missing.
(d) Consider whether the reaction is worth measuring. MsrA runs in both directions (Lim, You, Kim, Levine, PNAS 2011, doi 10.1073/pnas.1101275108), so an equilibrium constant against a calibrated thiol-disulfide redox buffer is experimentally reachable and would be the first measured value for this couple.
(e) Separately, r_4478 and r_4550 are a same-species diffusion and an exchange; they close by the pipeline's own code rules and were not investigated here.
